sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Think of them like spreadsheets or game boards where you can work with rows and columns.

• How to access and modify elements in 2D arrays
• Ways to loop through all elements efficiently
• Practical examples like finding sums or patterns

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine a chessboard. Each square has a row and column number, right? A 2D array works the same way!

• It's just an array of arrays (rows containing columns)
• You use two indices: `array[row][column]`
• Great for grids, tables, or any data with two dimensions

For example, a 3x3 tic-tac-toe board would be a 2D array where you can check each cell for X, O, or empty. Simple!

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Use nested for loops to traverse all elements of a 2D array
The outer loop iterates over rows; the inner loop iterates over columns
Common operations include summing elements, finding max/min, and printing the matrix
The enhanced for loop can also traverse 2D arrays: for (int[] row : matrix)
Row-by-row processing is the standard pattern for 2D array algorithms

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: 2D arrays are grids with rows and columns. Use nested loops to process all elements. Practice with real-world examples like spreadsheets or games. Ready to move on to passing 2D arrays to methods.
